scope: Manual review of the six remaining p0131 tensor PCA, CCA and Hermite interfaces.

rows.query: Search asymmetric tensor PCA and inspect pure-tensor coordinates, finite Gaussian law and repeated product sampling.
rows.result: Pure tensor coordinates plus a translated standard Gaussian law support the observation model, without a dedicated tensor-PCA interface.
rows.gap: The asymmetric model still needs the finite-array tensor identification, factor-norm constraints and exact translated iid Gaussian experiment.

comparisons.D3: Each of k distinct factors has Euclidean norm sqrt(d), so their product tensor has Frobenius norm sqrt(d^k); lambda/sqrt(d^k) sets signal norm lambda. Noise entries in all ordered index positions are independent real N(0,1), and samples are iid. The target is the product tensor, not the individual factors or one common repeated factor; no prior on these fixed unknown vectors is imposed.

rows.query: Search higher-order canonical correlation and inspect tensor product inner/coordinate identities and moment integration.
rows.result: The cross-moment tensor can be represented and integrated; the definition specifies a moment constraint rather than a complete Gaussian model.
rows.gap: The higher-order CCA model still needs an integrable cross-moment tensor and a joint law satisfying the stated rank-one expectation.

comparisons.D12: Each sample contains k views of dimension d, with E of their outer product=lambda V/sqrt(d^k), and V=sqrt(d^k) times unit-factor tensor product. Samples are iid, but views cannot be declared independent merely from this statement and their covariances are not specified as identities here. Preserve the uncentered kth cross moment rather than replacing it by a covariance or cumulant; D13 is a separate lower-bound subfamily, not the general CCA law.

rows.query: Inspect pure-tensor basis coordinates for a tensor product of coordinate vectors.
rows.result: The basis coordinate-product identity represents the one-coordinate-per-mode signal tensor.
rows.gap: The restricted signal class still needs its scaled coordinate-basis tensors with independently chosen mode indices.

comparisons.D14: Choose i1,...,ik in [d] and scale their standard-basis tensor product by sqrt(d^k). The printed set notation does not require the indices to be pairwise distinct; imposing that would change the class, especially when k>d. This is a restriction on signal tensors in the CCA model, not an asserted algorithm or a completed parity-learning reduction.

rows.query: Inspect density construction, Gaussian base law and sign at zero; compare the exact CCA likelihood-ratio normalization.
rows.result: A bounded sign perturbation can define a density relative to a Gaussian law, but the source's two formulas for lambda_k disagree.
rows.gap: The CCA subfamily still needs resolution of the inconsistent lambda_k formula and proofs of density normalization and the desired cross moment.

comparisons.D13: Use base N(0,I_kd) and density 1+(lambda/lambda_k) sign(inner(view tensor,V)/sqrt(d^k)); sign(0)=0. Nonnegativity follows when the chosen positive lambda_k bounds lambda; Gaussian symmetry supports normalization after measurability. The printed (2/pi)^(k/2) differs from (E|Z|)^(k/2), since E|Z|=sqrt(2/pi); the cross-moment calibration cannot treat both as equal. Preserve lambda=0 allowance here despite the general model's lambda>0 and do not replace the joint perturbed law by independent views.

rows.query: Search symmetric tensor PCA and inspect pure-tensor coordinates, translated Gaussian observations and finite iid products.
rows.result: The repeated-factor signal and independent ordered-entry noise have building blocks; the signal symmetry does not symmetrize the Gaussian tensor.
rows.gap: The symmetric model still needs its repeated-factor mean tensor and iid full-array Gaussian experiment with the vector parameter retained.

comparisons.D2: The unknown target is V in R^d of norm sqrt(d); mean is lambda V tensor-power k divided by sqrt(d^k). The signal is symmetric, but W has independent N(0,1) entries at all ordered indices, not a symmetric Gaussian tensor. Preserve N observations versus printed X_(1:m) discrepancy without inventing m as a second sample count. For even k the data cannot distinguish V and -V, which does not authorize changing the source parameter space.

rows.query: Search Hermite orthonormality and inspect probabilists' Hermite recursion, monicity and Gaussian derivative identity.
rows.result: The library provides monic probabilists' Hermite polynomials and their Gaussian derivative relation; these are not normalized to unit L2 Gaussian norm.
rows.gap: The orthonormal Gaussian polynomial family still needs factorial normalization and a proved multivariate product orthonormality/completeness bridge.

comparisons.D7: Polynomial.hermite n is integer-coefficient monic He_n, starting 1,x,x^2-1; normalized H_n requires scaling by 1/sqrt(n!) after real evaluation. Multivariate H_c uses products of normalized coordinate polynomials under a standard product Gaussian; neither monicity nor the derivative identity supplies that orthonormality theorem. The source's appendix background is excluded, so no additional convention or completeness claim is imported from it.
